newsitem.title: UK: N.Sea Brent prices weaker, active paper steady.
newsitem.headline: N.Sea Brent prices weaker, active paper steady.

text.p: North Sea crude prices were weaker on Thursday, echoing Wednesday's sharp losses on Brent futures and weaker sentiment for the physical market.
However, active paper play saw forward Brent spreads hold steady at slightly lower levels, traders said.
March Brent futures bounced, making early 20 cent gains after shedding around 60 cents late on Wednesday, but hovered around unchanged at $20.50 support in early afternoon trade.
Dated Brent were notionally about five cents weaker at March evens, but talk was thin and traders expect to see it slip into discount with little buying seen and the transatlantic arb shut.
March/April paper dipped to trade at +28 cents in overnight business but the early futures gains and active buying interest saw it widening out to trade around +33 cents over the morning.
Swaps, however, stayed under pressure, flagging the market's weaker sentiment. Next week's dates slipped to about April Brent +16/+19 cents after trade at +23 cents in early business.

The March Brent loading programme was set at the equivalent of 42 cargoes of 500,000 barrels and 1.93 million barrels in smaller top-up cargoes. This was up four cargoes from February's 38 standard cargoes plus 1.36 million barrels in top-ups.
Traders said the March programme was as expected.
In the Mediterranean Urals was notionally unchanged at Dated Brent -85/90 cents although sentiment was bearish, traders said.
A dearth of immediate supply with Novorossiisk remaining closed was balanced by lacklustre buying interest depressed by continuing poor refining margins.
Traders said the possible advent of Iraqi spot crude sales also hit sentiment while the bullish factor of the port closure was balanced by the long list of vessels waiting to load.
"People are not desperate for these cargoes," a trader said.
West African discussion was slowed by the marginal arb to the United States.
